data.title: China proposes stricter car design, testing rules, including ban on fully hidden door handles
data.description:
China's industry ministry on Saturday proposed tighter oversight of automakers' innovative designs and research and development testing. It said some manufacturers had rushed out new models without enough validation, which raised safety and environmental risks.

• From January 1, 2027, automakers seeking approval for new models must submit more technical details on innovative designs and testing. Models that are poorly tested or backed by false data will be rejected, the draft said

• Models that already have approval must file information on their innovative designs by July 1, 2027. If they do not and have safety hazards, automakers must halt production and recall them

• The draft bans fully hidden door handles and foldable or flexible displays. It also bars use of "zero-gravity" or swivel seats while driving

• Key functions such as lights and wipers must keep physical controls

• The ministry drafted the rules with three other agencies and is taking public comment until November 10

data.title: Adani Green Energy capacity rises 24% in April-September, energy sales up 32%
data.description:
Adani Green Energy's operational renewable energy capacity increased 24% year-on-year to 20,763 MW in the first half of FY27, while energy sales rose 32% to 25,747 million units, according to the company's provisional operational update released on October 10.

The company added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity during the April-September period. Of this, 621 MW was added during the second quarter of FY27.

The company also operationalised 3,081 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at Khavda in Gujarat during the July-September quarter, taking its total installed BESS capacity to 6,632 MWh as of September 30, 2026.

Adani Green Energy reported a capacity utilisation factor (CUF) of 22.9% for its solar portfolio, 42.9% for its wind portfolio and 45.2% for its hybrid portfolio during H1 FY27. Plant availability stood at 99.3% for solar, 94.6% for wind and 98.8% for hybrid projects.

The company said its operational portfolio powered more than 4.4 million homes and helped avoid 17.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions during the first half of FY27.

The operational update is provisional and covers the six months ended September 30, 2026.

data.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump announcement on diesel
data.description:
Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following US President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel.

"The federal government has taken note of the US decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement.

He said Germany's position remained clear: "The federal government remains committed to the decisions on sanctions against Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions."

He said Germany's support for Ukraine was unchanged and diplomatic efforts to reach a solution would continue.

Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. He said his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.

Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, have risen to near record levels, posing a risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who visited Kyiv last weekend, has said repeatedly that Germany, Ukraine's largest European donor, would not reduce its support for the Kyiv government.

data.title: KEC International bags new transmission and distribution orders worth ₹1,014 crore in India
data.description:
KEC International has secured new orders worth ₹1,014 crore in its India transmission and distribution (T&D) business, the company said on October 10.

The orders include the company's first order for setting up a 765 kV transmission line for the evacuation of power from a pumped storage plant (PSP) in Western India. The company described itself in the release as a global infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) major and an RPG Group company.

In a separate filing to the NSE and BSE, the company's secretary and compliance officer, Suraj Eksambekar, said all the orders mentioned in the press release were received in the normal course of business.

Commenting on the development, Vimal Kejriwal, managing director and chief executive officer of KEC International, said the company was delighted to secure the "prestigious" order from an existing client for the evacuation of power from a PSP.

He said it marked an important milestone for the T&D business, as the company supports the growing power infrastructure requirements of the renewables segment.

Kejriwal added that, with these wins, the company's year-to-date order intake stands at over ₹9,600 crore.

KEC International is a global infrastructure EPC major. It has a presence in the verticals of power transmission and distribution, civil, transportation, renewables, oil and gas pipelines, and cables and conductors. The company has a footprint in 110+ countries, which includes EPC and the supply of towers and cables. It is the flagship company of the RPG Group.

On the NSE, KEC International shares closed at ₹365.75, up ₹16.15, or 4.62%.

data.title: AAVE Jumps After Citrini Research Bets On DeFi Tokens’ $157T Tokenization Opportunity
data.description:
Key points:
  • Aave rose over 4% on Saturday, the clearest gainer among five DeFi tokens reportedly named in Citrini Research’s tokenization basket, while Bitcoin added only 0.2%.
  • Citrini argued that moving traditional assets onchain could expand trading, lending and payment markets.
  • The firm cautioned that higher onchain volume would not necessarily lift token prices, pointing instead to revenue models, fee allocation and token-holder participation.

Aave (AAVE) edged higher on Saturday, outperforming Bitcoin (BTC) and becoming the clearest gainer among five decentralized finance (DeFi) tokens Citrini Research reportedly named in its tokenization basket this week.

Citrini, an independent financial and thematic investment research firm, published the basket on Thursday, explaining that moving traditional assets onto blockchains could expand on-chain trading, lending and payment markets, according to a CoinDesk report. The scale gap was the starting point for the argument.

Citrini said the question for investors was not whether more assets get tokenized, but “where the economics accrue.” It described an onchain ecosystem that now ran from tokenized treasuries, equities, and options to programmable debt, lending, payments, and yield protocols - “entire financial applications that simply didn’t exist a few years ago.”

Bitcoin Extends Weekly Losses As Ether.fi Slides, Pendle And Uniswap Edge Higher

That distinction was showing up in the prices. While AAVE gained, the rest of the group barely moved. Pendle (PENDLE) gained 0.8%, and Uniswap (UNI) gained 0.3%, both only slightly ahead of Bitcoin, which was up only 0.2% in the last 24 hours. Ether.fi (ETHFI) went the other way, falling 5.5% over the past 24 hours.

Bitcoin’s price fell back to $82,761 at the time of writing. Over the week, Bitcoin has fallen over 2%, despite having reached the $86,000 range just last week.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

AAVE Rallies After MetaMask Integration Drives AI Trading Buzz

Aave's gain came as MetaMask's Agent Wallet was integrated with Aave's MCP, connecting the lending protocol to AI-driven transactions. The protocol also reported rising V4 deposits ahead of a deployment review and strong third-quarter growth.

AAVE’s price was up over 4% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around AAVE remained in the ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

What Citrini Named

According to the research firm, global equities were worth over $157 trillion against a crypto market capitalization of nearly $2.66 trillion, the firm said. It added that the on-chain value of tokenized stocks and equities had climbed to roughly $4.84 billion.

Citrini pointed to Robinhood (HOOD) Chain as the first to open the market with stock tokens, and noted that in the week ending Sept. 13, Solana’s (SOL) decentralized exchanges processed about 208 million trades against 190 million on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The firm also favored Coinbase (COIN), besides highlighting Hyperliquid (HYPE).

HOOD stock closed up by over 1% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HOOD remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

Volume Isn't Value

The firm was explicit that none of this guaranteed that the tokens would go up. Higher on-chain volume does not necessarily lift token prices, Citrini said. What mattered more was how a protocol earned revenue, where its fees went, and whether token holders shared in them.

Over a week, the picture was still weak.

Uniswap is down roughly 20% and Pendle 9%, against a 2% decline in Bitcoin.

data.title: RBI may raise repo rate by 75-100 bps in current cycle: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise the repo rate by 75-100 basis points in the current tightening cycle, with inflation expected to remain elevated before easing from the next financial year, according to an SBI Capital Markets report.

SBI Caps said gradual rate increases remain the base case, although a larger hike in December 2026 cannot be ruled out depending on inflation readings for September and October.

The report said the Monetary Policy Committee's 25-basis-point repo rate hike and its shift in stance from "Neutral" to "Calibrated Tightening" signal a stronger focus on containing inflation. It expects the policy cycle to turn around in the first quarter of FY28 as the growth-inflation balance evolves.

Consumer inflation is expected to peak in the third quarter of FY27, while wholesale price inflation could begin easing from March 2027 as favourable base effects set in. Consumer price inflation is likely to trend below 5 per cent year-on-year beyond Q1FY28, the report said.

India's economic growth has remained strong, with real gross domestic product (GDP) expanding 7.8 per cent year-on-year in Q1FY27, exceeding market expectations of 7.1 per cent. Manufacturing grew 9.2 per cent, while gross fixed capital formation rose 11.9 per cent during the quarter.

However, the brokerage flagged risks to consumption in the second half of FY27, including rising borrowing costs, subdued rural sentiment and weaker kharif sowing. It also warned that prolonged geopolitical conflicts and crude oil prices around USD 100 per barrel could sustain cost pressures.

The report noted benchmark 10-year government bond yields had risen around 70 basis points in calendar year 2026, with yields likely to remain elevated until geopolitical tensions ease and inflationary pressures moderate.

Higher interest rates are expected to support bank margins in the near term, although non-food credit growth could gradually slow towards the end of FY27. SBI Capital Markets expects FY27 to remain favourable for banks, while bonds could regain investor interest in FY28.

The report also highlighted global uncertainty, with rising yields in advanced economies and capital outflows from emerging markets adding to financial pressures.

data.title: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Demand Is Likely Slipping — But Gene Munster Says That’s Not The Real Story
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said iPhone 18 Pro lead times across eight countries initially came in significantly ahead of last year's iPhone 17 Pro, suggesting strong early demand for Apple's latest premium model.
  • However, he noted that the lead times have since fallen considerably further, which are 31% shorter now.
  • Munster acknowledged that the decline is concerning, but said some deterioration was expected because Apple's new iPhone Duo could pull consumers away from the Pro lineup.

Apple Inc.'s (AAPL) iPhone 18 Pro demand may be losing some momentum after a strong start, but Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster believes the latest data needs to be viewed in the broader context of Apple's new iPhone lineup.

Munster pointed to a key distinction between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as an early indicator of how consumers are responding to Apple's split product cycle.

Apple shares ended with a loss of over 1% in Friday’s regular trade and edged lower by another 0.2% in the afterhours session.

iPhone 18 Pro Lead Times Are Falling

Munster said iPhone 18 Pro lead times across eight countries initially came in significantly ahead of last year's iPhone 17 Pro, suggesting strong early demand for Apple's latest premium model.

On launch day, iPhone 18 Pro lead times were 15% longer than those for the iPhone 17 Pro a year earlier, he noted. They remained 15% higher after one week before falling to 5% below last year's levels at the two-week mark.

Munster said that the lead times have since fallen considerably further, which are 31% shorter now.

He acknowledged that the decline is concerning, but said some deterioration was expected because Apple's new iPhone Duo could pull consumers away from the Pro lineup.

"Going into the cycle, I predicted we would see lead times 20% lower than last year given the carrot of the new Duo would pull former Pro buyers up to the Duo," he said.

iPhone 18 Pro Max Holds Up Despite The Duo

While the iPhone 18 Pro has seen lead times fall sharply, the Pro Max has held up much better, Munster observed.

On launch day, iPhone 18 Pro Max lead times were 18% longer than the iPhone 17 Pro Max a year earlier. They remained 8% higher after one week and 6% higher after two weeks, he said. Today, they are still roughly in line with last year's levels, according to Munster, who termed this as a “win” for Apple, while noting that he expected the Duo to pull a meaningful portion of last year's Pro Max buyers away from the premium lineup.

"My guess is a sizable, maybe 20%, of last year's early Pro Max buyers are holding off for the Duo," he said.

If that is happening, Munster argues the stable Pro Max lead times could indicate that other iPhone buyers are moving up the product ladder instead.

One possibility is that consumers who would normally buy the standard iPhone 18 are choosing the Pro or Pro Max instead because the standard model will not ship until next spring. "In this case, that's a win for the FY27 iPhone revenue," Munster said.

That potential mix shift could become increasingly important as investors assess whether Apple's decision to split its iPhone launch cycle is actually working. The combined iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max lead times are currently averaging about three weeks, Munster said, which remains roughly in line with last year's combined figure. But he cautioned that the direction of the most recent data matters.

"The trend of the fast decline in recent weeks is more telling," Munster said, while highlighting that the next major test will come when Apple begins taking preorders for the iPhone Duo.

What Retail Traders Think Of AAPL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Apple trended in the ‘neutral’ territory at the time of writing.

AAPL stock is up 24% year-to-date and 33% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 16% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 23%.

data.title: Credit card overlimit facility: Eligibility, charges and 6 factors to consider before opting in
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- A sudden medical bill, surgery, or an unexpected expense can push an individual's credit card spending beyond its approved limit. In such cases, an overlimit facility may help you complete these transactions, but the extra spending can still come at a meaningful cost.

That is why, before opting in, credit cardholders should understand how the facility works, what fees may apply, and how using such a service can affect an individual's credit profile.

It is vital to keep in mind that, as of October 2026, major Indian financial institutions generally charge a credit card overlimit fee of about 2.5% on the amount exceeding the assigned credit limit, subject to a minimum charge of approximately Rs.500- Rs.600, along with applicable GST. This fee may vary by banking institution and credit card variant.

For example, SBI Card sets a minimum fee of Rs.600 for credit card overlimit charges, whereas HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank specify a minimum of Rs.550, Rs.500 and Rs.500, respectively.

That is why credit cardholders should check their respective banks' latest terms, eligibility requirements (if any) and associated conditions and refer to their official websites for complete details before availing of this facility.

To put it simply, a credit card overlimit facility permits a credit card holder to spend money beyond their assigned credit limit. This spending is permitted subject to the issuer's terms, approval and conditions. For example, if your credit limit is Rs.1 lakh, the facility may permit an eligible transaction that might take your total outstanding balance beyond this amount.

Still, it is essential to keep in mind that this facility is not 'automatic' and the issuer might also decline transactions or impose fines for exceeding the limit, as per their predetermined policies in such cases. This calls for a conceptual understanding of the credit card overlimit facility so that this facility can be utilised meaningfully to the advantage of a credit card holder.

As per the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, all card issuers are mandated to obtain clear and explicit consent from the respective credit card holder before extending an overlimit facility. In case the user opts out of this consent, such a facility cannot be extended to them. No fee can be imposed arbitrarily by the credit card issuing institution if the credit card holder did not voluntarily opt for this facility.

If an individual explicitly opts for this service, the terms and conditions of the respective credit card institution will apply. In such cases, banks may levy fees when an individual's outstanding balance exceeds the approved limit, depending primarily on their terms and applicable regulations. To gain complete clarity on this, credit card users should check the latest applicable fees, speak to the customer service team if they have doubts, and check whether charges apply only to the excess amount or on another specified basis.

This is yet another vital aspect that requires due consideration. This means that opting in alone does not guarantee that every transaction above an individual's credit card limit will be approved. Based on the terms, conditions, risk assessment and policies, the credit card issuing institution might still reject or withhold a transaction.

If you opt for the service, utilise funds, and do not repay the outstanding amount in full, this may increase your overall debt. To avoid late surprises, you should carefully review your credit cards' interest-free period rules and repayment terms, rather than simply ignoring these aspects and treating the facility as 'extra income'. In case of doubts, it is wise to first speak to the designated customer service team so that the facility is availed only after a complete understanding.

When you spend beyond your credit card limit, it can increase your credit utilisation ratio. Such a development can adversely affect your credit score. To put it simply, if your total credit limit is Rs.1 lakh, as a general guideline, you should keep your credit utilisation ratio to about 25-30% of this limit, i.e., Rs.25,000 to Rs.30,000. This is because higher utilisation can signal greater dependence on borrowed funds, particularly if it persists.

Finally, the total amount spent above your credit limit must also be repaid in accordance with the stipulations and regulations. Missing the repayment deadline, even delaying it by one day, can result in serious consequences, such as late-payment penalties, and can also decisively alter an individual's credit history.

In summary, a credit card overlimit facility can definitely provide flexibility to individual credit card holders during emergencies. Still, it should not be looked at as a substitute for adequate savings or careful budgeting.

One should consider opting into this service only after acknowledging and understanding the associated charges, interest costs, possible penalties, and long-term ramifications. Using it sparingly to avoid unnecessary debt is a wise way to handle this facility.

data.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
data.description:
By Jan Strupczewski and Foo Yun Chee

The European Union's long-term budget for the period 2028 to 2034 should be 8% lower than the European Commission's proposed €2 trillion, the Irish EU presidency said on Saturday.

This would result in a budget of €1.6 trillion, according to the Irish proposal, though it will be subject to contentious negotiations among EU countries in the coming months.

The proposal still marks a 30% increase over the current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027, and is certain to face stiff resistance from some countries such as Germany that want to keep a firm lid on spending.

The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies.

The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc will have to deal with new challenges such as spending more on defence and making Europe more competitive, while some EU countries want to retain most of the expenditure on old policies to support farming and regional development.

"The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal.

Ireland put the Commission's original €2 trillion figure at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction.

The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries spending from the Commission's own figures, and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness, prosperity and security.

It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties and selling CO2 emissions permits to companies, among other sources.

EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The ⁠EU budget, which is known as the Multiannual Financial Framework, needs to be agreed by all 27 member states.

While more frugally-minded countries such as Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordic countries have called for budget cutbacks, others including Spain, Italy and Poland are keen to protect expenditure.

data.title: The midterm strategy driving Democrats deep into Trump country
data.description:
Key points:
  • Democrats expand House battlefield into Trump territory
  • Strategy aims to stretch Republican resources and boost fundraising
  • Republicans dismiss the strategy as costly distraction

By Leah Douglas, Joseph Ax and Tim Reid

On paper, Democrat Justin Pearson, a 31-year-old Tennessee state legislator, has little chance of winning the state's 9th Congressional District, which Republican lawmakers redrew months ago from a Democratic stronghold to a deeply Republican seat.

Yet this week the national Democratic Party added the rural district to its list of midterm targets in November, part of a broader strategy to compete in President Donald Trump's conservative heartland despite long odds of flipping it.

On its face, the strategy may look like Democratic overreach. Voters living in the 9th District's newly reconfigured boundaries, for instance, picked Trump by more than 21 points in 2024.

More than a dozen Democratic operatives, strategists and candidates told Reuters the goal in part is to force Republicans to spend money defending safe seats, draining resources from the swing districts that will decide control of the US House.

By expanding the map, the party is also signaling to donors that races are becoming more competitive amid high prices and the Iran war driving Trump's unpopularity, helping unlock money that might otherwise stay on the sidelines, they said.

"These expansions force Republicans to go on defense in more districts," said one House campaign official, speaking on the condition of anonymity. "It's also a signal to donors and outside groups that House Democrats are taking these races seriously."

REPUBLICANS DISMISSIVE OF NEW MAP

The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, the party's US House campaign arm, this week added Pearson's race and 13 others to its target list, expanding its battlefield to 66 Republican-held seats.

Getting on the target list gives candidates access to national party staff and campaign tools, while also raising their profiles with donors, potentially opening new streams of fundraising for their campaigns.

There are early signs the strategy is having some effect. Republican-aligned groups have begun spending in some newly added districts, while two Democratic campaigns in Republican districts told Reuters their fundraising accelerated after being placed on the target list.

Republicans have dismissed the idea that Democrats have a serious chance of defeating their party in districts that overwhelmingly voted for Trump in 2024.

Mike Marinella, a spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee - the party's House campaign group - accused the Democratic Party of "stretching its map a mile wide and an inch deep, pretending every district in America is suddenly a battleground." He said the strategy will force Democrats to spend in long-shot contests when the party is already being outspent by Republicans.

Analysts, too, are skeptical.

"I'll take it seriously when they actually put their money where their mouth is. There is a point at which it becomes fantasy land," said David Wasserman, an elections analyst at the nonpartisan Cook Political Report, which rates many of these races as safely Republican.

Democrats say they have chosen these districts for a number of reasons, including the quality of their candidates and the chance they might pull off upset wins to increase the size of a potential House majority.

FOLLOWING THE MONEY

It remains unclear how much money Democrats will ultimately devote to the newly added districts. Recent campaign finance filings are not yet available, and the party declined to tell Reuters where it is spending or how much it plans to spend on its expanded map.

But there are signs Republicans are paying attention. Restoration of America PAC, funded primarily by billionaire Richard Uihlein, spent nearly $750,000 on digital ads backing Republican David Flippo in Nevada's 2nd District last week, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

The district, which Trump carried by 14 points in 2024, is among the recent additions to the Democratic target list.

"Democrats are on offense, Republicans are running scared, even in deep-red territory, and our expansive map reflects it," DCCC Chair Suzan DelBene said in a statement.

The new target list includes districts in Arkansas, New York and Virginia that Trump carried by as many as 24 points. Democrats say rising costs and dissatisfaction with some Trump policies are creating openings in rural and Republican-leaning areas.

"Rural America is unhappy with tariffs and rising fuel and farm costs, and that's pushing us into redder areas," Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said.

Democrats will need a net gain of four to retake the House. However, only about 50 of the 435 House races are expected to be competitive.

TENNESSEE DREAMING

Tennessee Republicans in May split the heavily Democratic Memphis area into three districts, transforming the 9th from a majority-Black urban seat into a sprawling district stretching more than 200 miles (322 km) across rural western Tennessee, a change that made the seat significantly more favorable to Republicans.

Yet Pearson says he has found independent and Republican voters frustrated by the high cost of living who are open to voting Democratic.

"We've traveled across all 15 counties, filling churches and community centers in places people said we couldn't compete," said Pearson, a Black lawmaker who gained national attention in 2023 when the Republican-majority legislature expelled him for joining a gun-violence protest at the state Capitol.

Republicans have portrayed Pearson as an outspoken progressive activist, pointing to his participation in gun-control and voting-rights protests.

"The people in Tennessee Nine, they have a clear choice. They can choose confidence over chaos, and they can choose common sense over communism, and they can choose a lawmaker over a troublemaker," his Republican opponent, state senator Brent Taylor, told Reuters.

There has been little public polling on the race, which Cook rates "Solid Republican."

EXCITE DONORS

Being added to the target list can quickly pay dividends for a campaign. Candidates or representatives from four Democratic campaigns on the DCCC's list told Reuters they either expected to see a boost in donations or were already seeing an uptick since their addition.

Pearson said his campaign has seen a surge of financial support after being added to the list, which would boost his get-out-the-vote operation.

"This race is going to be tight. It's going to be close. It's going to come down to how many people can we see before Election Day, knocking on those doors and reaching out to them directly," he said.

But Democrats' ambitions are constrained by a relative cash shortage.

While Democratic candidates nationally have outraised their Republican opponents, Republican national party committees and Republican-aligned super PACs have far outstripped Democratic counterparts in money raised.

Democrats in tough races in the expanded map said they are connecting with small-dollar donors by focusing on cost-of-living issues and campaigning heavily at town halls and other local appearances.

data.title: Diversifying Your Portfolio in the Age of AI Is Tricky. How to Do It. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Janna Herron

Diversifying your portfolio isn't as simple as it once was.

The artificial-intelligence boom is lifting many boats, including sectors and in regions typically driven by different fundamentals. AI-related stocks are the main driver behind many broad indexes. And even the traditional hedge to equities — the bond market — is moving with stocks.

What can an investor do? Dive deep into your current holdings to discover what you are exposed to, experts say. Then tweak your investments by finding assets that are less correlated with each other to spread the risk.

Here's how.

Take stock

Get under the hood of your investments in your 401(k) and other investment accounts. What funds do you hold? What do those funds include? And what's driving their returns?

"You really have to do the X-ray and know how much they overlap and how much you are exposed to the more volatile areas of the AI trade," said Patrick Huey, owner of Victory Independent Planning.

Even traditionally diverse index funds need a second look.

Many are designed to track the performance of a broad index, such as the S&P 500. But the index is capitalization weighted, meaning larger companies influence the index's performance more. Lately, those large companies are AI ones.

That is all well and good when those stocks are booming. But if — and when — they lead to a selloff, that leaves your portfolio overexposed to the AI trade.

"In 401ks, you're kind of forced into these index funds and so you're gonna take it on the chin if the market goes down," said Monica Dwyer, a senior vice president at Harvest Financial Advisors.

How to diversify with U.S. stocks

So let's diversify — starting with U.S. stocks.

One big factor to consider is how directly exposed a stock or sector is to the AI trade. While AI is buoying the fortunes of traditionally less correlated sectors like technology, utilities and real estate, the boost isn't uniform.

AI chip companies and memory chip manufacturers have the most direct exposure, whereas many areas of real estate — such as retail or multifamily — have much less.

Power companies, the energy demand from data centers, may fall in the middle.

"Utilities probably tend to become more correlated with technology and AI than we used to think," said Laura Mattia, senior vice president at Wealth Enhancement.

Then there are sectors like healthcare. While AI may eventually improve healthcare services or disease research, healthcare demand is largely driven by an aging population, a trend that continues to grow — with or without AI.

And if you want a large-cap index fund, "focus more on an equal-weighted one," Mattia said.

Look for mutual funds or exchange-traded funds like Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF that weights companies in the S&P 500 by revenue or Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF that gives each company the exact same weighting.

Go international

Investing in stocks abroad won't automatically diversify your portfolio now. U.S. equities make up roughly half of the global market, according to FactSet, and AI remains a big driver in overseas indexes.

So examine what your international holdings actually are. If you find too much AI exposure, maybe move away from those large-cap international stocks. Consider small-cap internationals instead.

"It's an interesting asset class that has done very well over the recent year or two," Mattia said. "They're more influenced by local behavior as opposed to the global economy."

Fix your fixed income

Don't forget to pore over your less risky assets like bonds.

"Historically you look for bonds to zig while stocks are zagging, and the reality is they're very highly correlated recently," said Catherine Valega, a certified financial planner at Green Bee Advisory.

Instead, Valega is turning to stable short-term liquid alternatives such as money-market funds, U.S. Treasury bills and certificates of deposit, or CDs, to fill out the conservative portion of her clients' portfolios.

"CDs are FDIC insured and Treasury bills are backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government, so why would I take a credit risk?" Valega said.

For corporate bonds, check out reinsurance or catastrophic bonds, which are influenced by natural disasters — and not larger economic trends.

"A tsunami in Asia has nothing to do with what the Federal Reserve decides at their next FOMC meeting," Mattia said, "so there it's just a different source of risk."

Think outside the box

Maybe it's time for some tried-and-true alternative assets — like commodities and precious metals. Take gold, for example.

"It has almost zero correlation to the U.S. stock market," said Matthew McKay, director of investments at Briaud Financial Advisors. "It has been a bit more correlated this past year but overall it's a pretty noncorrelated asset."

As for energy commodities, consider this: When stocks went gangbusters in recent years, energy commodities "blew it out of the water when you compare it," McKay said.

If your 401(k) doesn't offer a commodity fund, try a precious metals equity fund, McKay said.

"When gold's performing well, gold-mining stocks are like double, triple that type of performance," he said, "so it's a good diversifier from that perspective."

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO: What does listing of Reliance Industries' company mean for Airtel, Vodafone, Indus Towers shares?
data.description:
Jio Platforms IPO, Oct. 10 -- The listing of Jio Platforms is likely introduce transformative structural shifts for both the broader Indian telecom sector and its parent company, Reliance Industries (RIL).

Amid growing anticipation around Jio Platforms' initial public offering (IPO), a fresh update on the issue has emerged. The Mukesh Ambani-led telecom company is likely to price its shares in the range of Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 apiece, Bloomberg reported, citing sources. However, Jio Platforms has not yet officially disclosed key details of the IPO, including the price band, valuation and timeline.

Jio's proposed valuation could reset the way investors assess Bharti Airtel, which has been a major beneficiary of improving average revenue per user (ARPU), tariff increases and industry consolidation.

Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, said Jio's standalone listing would establish a transparent valuation benchmark for the telecom sector and could trigger a re-rating of listed peers, including Airtel.

At a reported valuation of around Rs.11 lakh crore, Jio Platforms would be valued slightly above Airtel's market capitalisation of approximately Rs.10.87 lakh crore. Garg noted that Jio's reported valuation of around 37 times FY26 profit compares with about 63 times trailing earnings for Airtel.

Meanwhile, Gaurav Garg, Head of Research at Lemonn, said Jio's listing could create a near-term overhang for the stock as investors compare the valuations of the two telecom giants.

Garg further explained that this valuation gap could influence institutional investors looking for direct exposure to Jio. Some investors may rebalance their portfolios ahead of the IPO, potentially creating short-term volatility in Airtel shares.

Beyond valuation, the Jio IPO could have a more lasting impact on the sector if it improves the prospects of another round of mobile tariff increases.

Srivastava expects structural tariff increases to become more likely once Jio's listing is completed and Vodafone Idea concludes its fundraising plans. She pointed to expectations of a roughly 15% tariff hike by December 2026, which could materially improve revenue and profitability across the industry.

India has not had a mobile tariff hike since July 2024, and a listed Jio will face minority shareholders every quarter. That raises the odds of the 12-15% hike the street has been waiting for.

Garg believes Jio's transition into a publicly listed company could strengthen this possibility. As a listed entity, Jio would face greater scrutiny from minority shareholders and the market over its financial performance, profitability and capital allocation.

"Jio's listing turns India's price-setter into a company that answers to shareholders every quarter, and that is the best case for the next tariff hike," Garg said.

A tariff increase could benefit Airtel and Vodafone Idea by lifting revenue per user without requiring a proportionate increase in their subscriber bases.

"Vodafone Idea could see a particularly significant percentage improvement because of its weaker financial position, although higher tariffs alone would not resolve its debt burden, funding needs and network investment requirements," said Srivasatava.

Srivasatava further explained that because Jio's initial free float is expected to be a tight 3%, massive immediate capital rotations out of established players remain unlikely.

For RIL shareholders, the IPO represents a major value-unlocking event. While RIL will transition back to being evaluated primarily on its retail, petrochemical, and new energy verticals, its retained 66.4% promoter stake in Jio will likely attract a holding company discount of 18% to 36%, though much of this is already priced into the stock, she said.

"Ultimately, the fresh equity raised will be channeled toward prepaying telecom debt, strengthening Jio's balance sheet as it cements its leadership in India's digital ecosystem," she added.

data.title: Rwanda Inflation Hits Over 3-Year High
data.description:
Rwanda's overall inflation rate accelerated for the sixth straight month to 20.0% in September 2026 from 15.9% in August, marking the fastest increase since June 2023.

The acceleration came as inflation for food and non-alcoholic beverages, the largest component of the inflation basket, surged to 25.2%, the highest since September 2023, from 16.7% in August. Inflation also accelerated for communications (29.1% vs 27.6% in August), restaurants and hotels (16.0% vs 13.7%), furnishings (10.8% vs 10.2%), and clothing and footwear (5.3% vs 5.0%).

Meanwhile, inflation eased for transportation (26.0% vs 27.5% in August) and housing and utilities (19.1% vs 19.9%).

On a monthly basis, the CPI rose by 5.0%, following a 2.6% gain in the prior month, marking the fastest pace in five months.

data.title: Aerodrome rallies 48% in four weeks, outpacing Bitcoin and Ether
data.description:
Aerodrome's AERO token has climbed approximately 48% over the past 30 days. The move puts it ahead of both Bitcoin and Ether over the same stretch, according to The Defiant.

The timing is not subtle. Aerodrome, the leading decentralized exchange on Coinbase's Base layer-2 network, is roughly two weeks away from merging with Velodrome Finance. Traders appear to be positioning early.

AERO has traded between $0.68 and $0.84 in early October 2026.

Aerodrome holds about $393 million in total value locked on Base. Total value locked, or TVL, is the pool of crypto deposited into a protocol's smart contracts.

Broader estimates place Aerodrome's TVL between $390 million and $411 million as of early October 2026. Most of that sits on Base.

Add Velodrome to the picture and the combined TVL comes to around $422 million as of October 9, 2026. This is less a merger of equals and more Aerodrome absorbing a sibling.

The token split makes that hierarchy explicit. Of the new supply, 94.5% goes to Aerodrome stakeholders. Velodrome stakeholders receive the remaining 5.5%.

The combination is scheduled to begin on October 21, 2026, at 8:00 p.m. ET. The two exchanges will fold into a single new protocol called Aero, designed to run across multiple Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) chains.

Token holders get converted, not wiped out. Existing AERO swaps into the new AERO at a 1:1 ratio. VELO holders receive about 0.044 new AERO per token.

Legacy token emissions will stop as part of the transition.

Post-merger, holders of sAERO will see real-time reward allocation replace the current weekly voting system. The new setup directs 100% of protocol revenue to participants.

The pitch for the merger is market reach. The combined protocol targets a broader addressable market worth over $63 billion across EVM ecosystems, up from the previous $7 billion.

Aerodrome launched on Base in late August 2023. It quickly became a top liquidity hub on the network, driven by vote-escrowed tokenomics and its fee mechanisms.

Vote-escrow is a design where users lock tokens for a period of time in exchange for governance power and a share of rewards. The longer the lock, the bigger the say.

The merger was first revealed in November 2025. It was initially targeted for Q2 2026. That window came and went, and the date has since landed on October 21.

data.title: Airlines ask Mumbai airport for terminal 1 structural safety reports
data.description:
Airlines have asked Mumbai airport to share structural safety reports of terminal 1 (T1) ahead of October 13 meeting to firm up reduction of flights.

The meeting is being held following intervention of the Civil Aviation Ministry which put on hold reduction of 265 international flights from October 26. On October 1 Mumbai International Airport Limited ( MIAL) proposed reduction of the flights in view of planned redevelopment of T1 due to safety concerns.

In a letter to MIAL, the Airline Operators Committee (AOC) has asked for an update on structural safety of T1. “There have been references to structural safety of T1 by MIAL at various forums. The AOC would like to review independent consultant reports that established such concerns,” it has said.

The airlines have also asked for a detailed redevelopment plan for T1, including its scope, phase wise execution plan and firm timelines.

While airlines are supporting safe and timely development of T1, AOC has requested for details of actual capacity utilisation of terminal 1 and 2 along with declared capacity.

“The AOC member airlines wish to place on record that the proposed 33 per cent reduction (of flights) has not be discussed with or agreed by the AOC committee or the affected AOC member airlines and is currently being proposed as an unilateral measure,” it said.

MIAL in its October 1 letter had said airlines were called for stakeholder meeting on September 16. “A number of airline partners chose not to participate in the meeting. MIAL nevertheless remains committed to continued stakeholder engagement and reiterates that the development programme and implementation timelines remain unchanged,” it said.

Mumbai airport has planned to redevelop a portion of terminal 1B from January 2027. The airport has said the terminal is 60 years old and is need of repairs. It said the partial closure of terminal 1B will impact not impact 90 per cent of city’s air traffic. Further it has said the airlines have been an option to temporarily relocate operations to Navi Mumbai.

data.title: One Acre of Yosemite Has Kicked Off a Battle Over the Future of National Parks — WSJ
data.description:
By Kate King

A sliver of meadow and trees on the edge of Yosemite National Park has become an unlikely battleground over whether development is allowed in national parks.

The National Park Service recently signed a preliminary agreement for a land swap with a Las Vegas developer. Under the arrangement, the federal government would give about an acre on the western boundary of Yosemite National Park's nearly 750,000-acre expanse, nestled in California's Sierra Nevada.

That would allow developer Jeff Pori to build a short road into the park from his adjacent property. Without it, he said, guests at the rustic resort Pori is planning would have to drive about 45 minutes along winding dirt roads to reach the park's main entrance.

In exchange, Pori agreed to transfer to the National Park Service a similarly valued piece of property located elsewhere in California.

He said his project would add needed lodging to the popular park, allowing more people to enjoy it.

"I remember a lot of hiking and a lot of streams and rivers around there," said Pori, who grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area and camped in Yosemite with friends and family as a child. "It's just like heaven, really."

News of the proposed land exchange set off a fury among conservationists, former Yosemite officials and many members of the public. Cicely Muldoon, a former superintendent of Yosemite, said the swap would set a dangerous precedent by signaling that protected natural spaces can be bartered away to private interests.

"It's not a piece of land that you use for real-estate transactions," Muldoon said.

Pori's attorney Lanny Davis said he has received so many threatening notes that he hit his iPhone's limit for blocking email addresses.

The blowback shows how fiercely protective Americans are of their national parks — particularly the "crown jewels" such as Yosemite, best known for its dramatic waterfalls — and how some consider any move toward private development to be crossing a line.

The Trump administration has a different view. It has been willing to consider opening up protected federal land to private developers and businesses. Most recently, Trump administration officials considered a request from Major League Baseball to host a game at a national park, possibly Grand Teton in Wyoming. In a letter to local officials sent earlier this month, MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said the league won't pursue the idea due to opposition from the local community.

Last year, the administration formed a task force to identify federal land that could be used to build affordable housing in an effort to address the nation's housing shortage.

Federal agencies are also pursuing proposed land exchanges with private landowners. In Texas, a federal judge recently allowed a proposed land swap between the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Elon Musk's SpaceX to proceed.

In Georgia, the National Park Service has signed preliminary agreements to give federal land to two private landowners on Cumberland Island, a federally protected barrier island wilderness, in exchange for privately owned parcels in ecologically sensitive areas.

Some land exchanges involving national parks have happened over the years, including an agreement with a public utility in the Everglades and a swap that allowed the island of St. John to build a public school on a parcel of the Virgin Islands National Park.

But conservationists say that land exchanges have historically been used only to expand the boundaries of federal parkland.

"Now they're using that same authority to break off pieces of the park to benefit a private developer," said Ed Stierli, vice president of government affairs for the nonpartisan advocacy group National Parks Conservation Association.

In 2024, Pori purchased 83 acres just outside the boundary of Yosemite. The property, known as Hazel Green Ranch, is an undeveloped parcel of meadowland. The famous naturalist John Muir wrote about visiting the "charming spot" during his excursion through the Sierra in the summer of 1869.

Pori, through his real-estate firm Kingsbarn Realty Capital, wants to build something similar to what Hazel Green Ranch's former owner had proposed: a 150-room lodge and cabins scattered around the meadow's perimeter.

But for the business to work, he needs to build a 700-foot-long road across federal land connecting his property to the Big Oak Flat Road leading into Yosemite.

Pori knew getting approval would be an uphill battle. He is friends and business partners with Russell Geyser, the son of Hazel Green Ranch's previous owner, Lewis Geyser, who previously lost a five-year legal battle over the issue.

Pori said he first asked Yosemite officials two years ago for an easement that would allow him to build his proposed road and was told "no." He and Davis then met last year with officials from the Interior Department, who offered a possible solution: a land exchange.

Critics have pointed to Pori's political contributions, which total $4,700, to Republican campaigns and candidates, including Trump, as evidence that his request may have received special consideration.

The Interior Department's press office said there was no political pressure to reach a predetermined outcome on the exchange, which is still far from finalized. Pori and Davis said they never sought political favors.

"We went through the system as it's designed to be used," Davis said. "Checked the boxes to get it done legally."

Even if the land exchange moves forward, Pori faces a long process before he can get approval for his proposed development.

"I bought this with absolutely no guarantee," he said. "I knew that going in."

Write to Kate King at kate.king@wsj.com

data.title: Godrej DEI Lab Launches Gateway Returnship Programme
data.description:
The initiative aims to help women return to work after career breaks through structured onboarding, coaching and cohort-based learning

Godrej DEI Lab, the diversity, equity and inclusion arm of the Godrej Industries group, has launched Gateway, a returnship programme designed to help experienced women professionals re-enter the workforce after career breaks linked to motherhood, marriage or caregiving. The initiative was announced at the finale of the second edition of India Included on Campus 2026, a case study competition focused on workplace inclusion. It aligns with the group’s target of achieving 40% inclusion of women, LGBTQIA+ individuals and people with disabilities by 2031.

Structured Return To Work

Gateway is designed to create a more structured route for professionals returning after extended career breaks. The programme includes structured onboarding, cohort-based learning and coaching to help participants integrate into mainstream hiring and workplace teams.

The initiative focuses on making career re-entry more accessible to experienced professionals whose skills may remain relevant despite time away from formal employment. It also seeks to address challenges associated with returning to mid-management roles, where employers may need to reassess experience, skills and readiness after a career break.

Sumit Mitra, Group Head of Human Resources and Corporate Services at Godrej Industries, said the programme aims to bring experienced mid-management talent back into the workforce and make return-to-work opportunities more visible.

Career Breaks Among Women

The programme draws on findings from the 2026 study The Missing Half, which highlights that 74% of educated women in India take career breaks. The study was used as a reference point for the case study competition, which asked students to examine barriers faced by women seeking to return to work.

Career interruptions linked to caregiving and family responsibilities can affect professional continuity and access to opportunities. Returnship programmes seek to provide a formal pathway for candidates to demonstrate their capabilities and transition back into employment.

B-School Teams Develop Solutions

The second edition of India Included on Campus 2026 brought together students from institutions including IIM Lucknow, IIT Delhi, XIM Bhubaneswar and SIBM Pune. Participants were asked to develop proposals addressing challenges faced by women returning to professional roles.

XIM Bhubaneswar emerged as the winning team, receiving a cash prize of Rs 1 lakh for its proposal for a structured returnship framework.

Parmesh Shahani, Head of Godrej DEI Lab, said the initiative was intended to translate ideas on inclusion into workplace solutions supported by peer networks and leadership involvement.

Focus On Workplace Inclusion

Gateway adds a return-to-work component to Godrej Industries’ broader inclusion target for 2031. Its implementation will be relevant to how employers structure recruitment, onboarding and support for professionals returning after career breaks.

The programme also highlights the role of employer-led initiatives in addressing gaps between experienced talent and available employment opportunities.

data.title: RBI Tightens Forex Rules As Rupee Trades Near Record Low
data.description:
The central bank has restricted the rebooking of cancelled rupee-linked derivative contracts and introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a series of measures to support the rupee, which is trading close to its all-time low, including a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three state-run oil marketing companies (OMCs).

The facility will cover Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOC), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL). It will take effect from 12 October 2026 and remain in place until further notice, the central bank said in a press release on Saturday.

Under the arrangement, the RBI will sell dollars to the three public sector OMCs through designated banks to meet their daily foreign currency requirements.

Restrictions On Forex Derivatives

The RBI has also introduced regulatory measures for the foreign exchange market, including restrictions on the rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the Indian rupee.

“Authorised Dealers shall not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving INR, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, which has been cancelled with any Authorised Dealer after the issuance of the Directions,” the RBI said.

However, the rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted.

The central bank has also reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions without establishing an underlying exposure to USD 5 million from USD 100 million.

The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, without establishing an underlying exposure, has also been lowered to USD 5 million equivalent from USD 100 million. The revised threshold applies across all recognised stock exchanges taken together.

New Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve

The RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR), requiring forex dealers to maintain a reserve equivalent to 20 per cent of the notional amount of each eligible derivative transaction involving the rupee.

The reserve will apply to foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee that are undertaken to hedge current account exposures, where the user purchases foreign currency against the rupee.

The RBI said the measures were intended to strengthen market discipline and ensure appropriate risk management in the foreign exchange market, while maintaining an orderly and transparent market environment.

Rupee Under Pressure

The rupee has depreciated by 6 per cent since the West Asia conflict began in late February. Over the past year, the Indian currency has declined by more than 8 per cent.

The RBI has been intervening heavily in the foreign exchange market to curb volatility and limit pressure on the currency.

India's foreign exchange reserves declined by around USD 51.1 billion in the four weeks ended 2 October, after reaching a record USD 785.7 billion in the week ended 4 September.

The latest measures come amid sustained pressure on the rupee and a decline in the country's foreign exchange reserves.

data.title: India Office Market Absorption Rises 26% In Q3 As Supply Hits Record High: CW
data.description:
GCCs accounted for 42 per cent of quarterly leasing, while Bengaluru and Hyderabad led overall office space demand

India’s office sector recorded net absorption of 14.1 million square feet (MSF) across the top eight cities in Q3 2026, rising 26 per cent quarter-on-quarter, even as a sharp increase in new completions pushed overall vacancy higher, according to Cushman & Wakefield’s Q3 2026 Office MarketBeat report.

Gross Leasing Volume (GLV) across the eight cities stood at 21.9 MSF during the quarter, up 3 per cent quarter-on-quarter, while leasing during the first nine months reached 64.6 MSF, the highest-ever volume recorded for the period. Fresh leasing accounted for around 75 per cent of YTD activity, while pre-commitments increased to around 12 per cent as occupiers sought to secure quality space ahead of project completions.

Hyderabad recorded the highest net absorption at 4.1 MSF, accounting for 29 per cent of the pan-India total and marking its strongest quarterly level since Q4 2021. Bengaluru followed closely with 4.02 MSF, contributing 28.6 per cent of overall absorption, while Delhi NCR recorded 2.2 MSF and Mumbai reported 1 MSF during the quarter.

Bengaluru also led gross leasing activity with 5.2 MSF in Q3, followed by Hyderabad at 4.2 MSF, Mumbai at 3.9 MSF and Delhi NCR at 3.8 MSF. YTD net absorption across the eight cities stood at 36.7 MSF, reflecting sustained occupier activity across India’s major office markets.

New office completions reached an all-time quarterly high of 22.7 MSF in Q3, nearly doubling from the previous quarter, with Bengaluru accounting for 43 per cent of additions and Hyderabad contributing another 38 per cent. Together, the two markets accounted for more than four-fifths of the new supply added during the quarter.

YTD supply stood at 43.3 MSF, equivalent to 82 per cent of the entire supply added during 2025, putting 2026 on course to become the highest-supply year on record. Pan-India vacancy subsequently increased 63 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 14.37 per cent, marking the first rise after twelve consecutive quarters of compression.

Despite the rise in vacancy, pan-India office rents increased 2 per cent quarter-on-quarter across most major markets. The report said sustained rental momentum alongside significant new supply additions reflected continued occupier demand for quality office spaces across key markets.

GCCs Drive Office Demand

Global Capability Centres (GCCs) remained a key source of office demand, leasing 9.1 MSF during Q3 and accounting for 42 per cent of total quarterly GLV. Bengaluru and Pune recorded particularly strong GCC concentration, with the segment contributing around 65 per cent of leasing activity in each market.

YTD GCC leasing reached 25.3 MSF, accounting for 39 per cent of total leasing, while GCCs contributed more than half of leasing activity in Bengaluru, Chennai and Pune. This highlights the broadening geographic footprint of GCC demand across India’s major office markets.

Anshul Jain, Chief Executive – India, SEA, MEA & APAC Office and Retail, Cushman & Wakefield, said, “India’s office market remains structurally strong, and the sustained levels of absorption and leasing we are seeing are a clear reflection of that. With 64.6 MSF of leasing in the first nine months of 2026, the highest ever for this period, the market continues to demonstrate remarkable depth and resilience, despite persistent macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.”

BFSI Leads Sector Demand

BFSI emerged as the largest sectoral demand driver in Q3, accounting for 24 per cent of total leasing activity, followed by IT-BPM at 22 per cent. On a YTD basis, BFSI leasing stood at 13.2 MSF, registering 34 per cent year-on-year growth, while IT-BPM occupiers leased approximately 14 MSF during the period.

Engineering and Manufacturing recorded its highest-ever YTD leasing volume at 10.2 MSF, while flexible workspace operators leased 3.5 MSF in Q3, accounting for 16 per cent of quarterly GLV. Flexible workspace leasing reached a record 11.9 MSF during the first nine months, rising 42 per cent year-on-year and accounting for 18 per cent of total leasing activity.

The first nine months of 2026 saw total leasing reach 64.6 MSF, around 74 per cent of the full-year 2025 volume, keeping the market on track for another strong year. The increase in pre-commitments also indicates that occupiers are planning ahead and securing space before new projects are completed.

data.title: The U.S. Army's Desert Tech Test Shows Long Road to AI Warfare — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Somerville | Photography by Ethan Swope for WSJ

Under a blistering desert sun, the U.S. Army strained to show it had become a modern, AI-powered fighting force.

Some blamed the heat. It was July in the Mojave Desert, and the thermometer climbed toward 110 degrees. Servers overheated. Batteries died and couldn't be recharged. Soldiers drenched T-shirts in ice water and draped them over antennas that were on the fritz.

Sgt. Ramontez Bennett's drone from Anduril Industries was supposed to loiter overhead. Instead, the relentless glare forced it to land. "They gotta do something about it overheating," he said. Plenty of America's conflicts have played out in temperatures rivaling this particular July day.

It wasn't just the sun causing problems. "All it takes is one gust of wind and it's on the side of a mountain," he said. Behind the rugged peaks, drones lost their signal.

Next to Bennett, another pilot prepared to launch a drone from Theiss UAV Solutions. After a prolonged wait to charge a drained battery, the aircraft took another 10 minutes to get airborne. Ukrainian soldiers can get a drone of about the same size off the ground in under a minute.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year threw down the gauntlet with a directive to transform the Army into an AI-powered force equipped with drones and 3-D printers to quickly spin up weapons components, and directed the service to buy more software and startup tech. He instructed the Defense Department to stop looking for perfection in its tech, and buy off-the-shelf products that are good enough, stressing the urgency of modernizing.

America's investments in such weapons, some of which date to the Biden administration, have slowly begun to change the way it fights. In Iran, a war that has relied largely on older and expensive systems, the U.S. also used an unmanned boat made by defense startup Saronic to rescue a stranded helicopter crew. A drone modeled on Iran's Shahed has been among the military's most successful low-cost offensive weapons. The drone, called Lucas, costs $10,000 to $55,000 a unit thanks to an arrangement in which the Pentagon owns the design and farms out production to a group of manufacturers.

Artificial-intelligence tools have also greatly accelerated intelligence analysis and target selection. The rapid evolution of the fighting in Ukraine shows how central such technologies will be to future wars.

But America's soldiers are still far from reaping the full benefits of cutting-edge autonomous weapons and AI systems, and haven't been forced by necessity to quickly modernize as militaries like Ukraine's have in the heat of conflict, current and former national-security officials said. Transforming a land-based fighting force with a history of slow technological adaptation into a nimble organization that makes the most of new innovations has been difficult.

Startups' emerging new tech, most of which has never been to war, has at times proven to be too brittle in real-world applications, soldiers said. The Army is also in the throes of upgrading battlefield connectivity and communications, steps that are key to being able to fully capitalize on next-generation weaponry.

The military has held at least five press calls in recent weeks to talk about its modernization efforts. "There is a recognition that the battlefield is changing before our eyes," Col. Gregory Merkl told reporters on one such call. "We are absolutely dedicated to transformation."

Fort Irwin

Project Convergence brought 9,700 infantry soldiers to the desert for a 10-day, round-the-clock mock fight against an Army unit called Blackhorse, which stood in for China's People's Liberation Army. Media briefing materials billed the three-day July trip as a glimpse "inside the U.S. Army's AI-enabled battlefield" and an opportunity for its leadership to demonstrate the use of AI apps, a data integration program, aerial and ground drones and sensor-loaded headsets in battle.

In some of the moments meant to spotlight advanced technology on the battlefield, newly procured drones and developmental communication systems failed to perform as intended.

Soldiers flew drones during limited windows and for half the maximum flight time to conserve battery and avoid losing them, and without full autonomy or any AI to assist. Chinese consumer drones could do the manual job a decade ago.

The battle offered the familiar scene of legacy warfare: green-suited soldiers kicking in doors, screaming above gunfire, weighed down with weapons from the last century.

An Army spokesman for Project Convergence said the event was designed to allow for specific units to experiment with drones during pockets of fighting and learn about the tech, not to flood the airspace with autonomous weapons. The event was a way to "fact-check all the vendors that are coming to us" about the veracity of sales pitches from a crop of defense technology firms, said Alex Miller, chief technology officer to the Army's chief of staff.

The Army found during the exercise that the augmented-reality headsets referenced in its media invitation to Fort Irwin showed some deficiencies and the service is uncertain if it would move forward with them, a senior defense official at the training event said. Three companies have won contracts each worth more than $100 million to build the headsets.

While much of the tech there had already been awarded sizable Army contracts, officials and soldiers involved described it as experimental rather than essential new weaponry.

"You take a piece of electronics and lay it out on a hot rock in 109 degree temperatures and try and make it work," said Lt. Gen. Michael McCurry, one of the senior Army leaders running the event. "We're seeing some of that."

An Anduril spokesman said its drone overheated and that it had previously been tested in hot and cold temperatures. Following soldiers' feedback, the company has prioritized making upgrades to improve the drone's performance in extreme environments, he said.

Theiss UAV Solutions founder Shawn Theiss said his drone typically launches within three minutes and that he received mostly positive feedback from soldiers at the exercise. Delays sometimes happen if soldiers aren't trained, or if the communications parts, made by a separate company, have glitches, he said. The Theiss UAV drones there were more than three years old and batteries may not have been at peak performance, which can affect the launch, he said.

Some defense officials said the efforts would bear fruit longer term despite near-term stumbles.

Modernizing the military

Congress has long hammered the Army about modernizing its fighting. Congressional probes and government oversight reports have found that the Army has wasted billions of taxpayer dollars on fumbled new weapons programs, and suffered from inadequate training and failures in cybersecurity and data management.

The Ukraine war brought the inadequacies into focus, bringing fully autonomous warfare to the battlefield with a tech proficiency that at times humbled the U.S. During battlefield drills held in Germany earlier this year, Ukraine's drone operators took out a U.S. armored brigade.

"The tech is moving so quickly that the U.S. military bureaucracy cannot keep up," said Jonathan Rue, a former deputy assistant secretary of defense who played a key role in getting new technology into the Army, and is now a partner at firm MVP Ventures.

The last major Army transformation came about in the 1980s, when the service pivoted from Vietnam and built the force it would use in the Gulf War. It retrained, reorganized and brought in armored fighting vehicles, attack helicopters and modern air defense systems.

The struggle now is to transform what recently ousted Army Sec. Dan Driscoll has called a "calcified bureaucracy" in preparation for a technologically sophisticated adversary — China. Driscoll departed in September, following disagreements with Hegseth.

Daniel Goure, a former military analyst with the Lexington Institute who has held numerous war college teaching positions and roles in the Defense Department, said the Army's history of modernization efforts are "almost unblemished by success." He blames a tradition of risk aversion and a hierarchical organization.

Still, upgrades like the Army's Next-Generation Command and Control system, used for AI-enabled planning and logistics, are a start. The system, with a $4 billion price tag in this year's budget, allows troops to move faster and in a more dispersed fashion over longer stretches of battlefield, which is essential in modern conflicts, Army officials say.

Starlink connectivity has meant that for the first time in his 19-year Army career, Lt. Col. Shawn Scott can radio a soldier sitting in an air-conditioned operations center at another end of the base, without cumbersome transmission poles. And new data-sharing technology has cut by two-thirds the time it takes Scott to plan and communicate missions.

The next step is bolstering the reliability of communications and data integration systems so AI-powered weaponry can actually help human fighters out in remote and austere conditions.

The Fort Irwin fighting climaxed with a predawn attack on a fabricated city, Razish, a relic of training for the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. Stryker armored combat vehicles rolled down the hills. Smoke trucks attempted to obfuscate the view. Mortar rounds exploded and soldiers moved from one building to the next, firing blank bullets and pausing for the occasional smoke break.

A swarm of five small drones was forced to turn back as three Black Hawk helicopters carrying senior Army officials flew into the same airspace, squandering a rare high-tech moment they had come to see.

"It'd be a very dangerous time for us just to hand over everything to technology," said Brig. Gen. Daniel Hibner, commander of the Army's Joint Modernization Command. "It's very much still a human endeavor."

data.title: AGES Austria issues GMP certification to Shilpa Medicare’s Jadcherla unit
data.description:
Shilpa Medicare’s Unit 4 in Jadcherla, Telangana, has received GMP certification from AGES, Austria, following a successful inspection, the company said in a regulatory filing on October 10.

The unit was inspected by AGES, Austria, from July 27, 2026 until July 30, 2026. Following the inspection, the Austrian agency issued the GMP certification.

According to the filing, Unit 4 is engaged in the manufacturing, testing and distribution of finished dosage forms. These include sterile injections and non-sterile tablets and capsules. The products are supplied to Europe and the rest of the world markets.

The company is headquartered in Raichur, Karnataka.

OERIS injection approval

In a separate development, Shilpa Medicare has received final approval from the Subject Expert Committee (SEC) under the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) to market OERIS, its extended-release ondansetron injection, in India.

The formulation is designed to provide protection against chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting for up to 120 hours, or five days, after a single dose.

The approval follows the successful completion of a Phase III clinical trial evaluating the drug’s safety and efficacy in patients undergoing moderately to highly emetogenic chemotherapy.

Shilpa Medicare plans to launch OERIS commercially across India after receiving the final marketing authorisation. The product is protected by a patent in India until 2039.

On the NSE, Shilpa Medicare shares closed at ₹1,025.70, up ₹0.40, or 0.04%.
